probeAttempts.entry: openclaw_runtime/src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts:532 dispatchInboundMessageWithBufferedDispatcher (the shared inbound entry behind desktop chat and the channel fixture)
probeAttempts.observed: no stdout for 120000ms; the vitest no-output watchdog terminated the stalled process group before any assertion ran
probeAttempts.conclusion: not a config-only fixture: the entry needs a channel plugin, session store and agent workspace harness; no test in the repo drives a gateway chat send end to end

observed: the model boundary was never reached: the fetch spy logged zero requests before the stall

a 5s heartbeat printed the active resources once (12-20 recursive FSEventWrap watchers plus Timeouts) and then stopped firing, so the event loop is blocked synchronously rather than awaiting something
moving process.cwd() to a temp directory under the forks pool (where chdir is supported) did not change the stall, so repo-shaped CWD scanning is not the cause
the per-test timeout never fired because a blocked event loop cannot run its timer
followUpProbe.conclusion: the blocker is synchronous work inside the runtime bootstrap (plugin/workspace loading) that a minimal config does not bound; a driver needs the repo's own bounded harness or a pre-warmed bootstrap, not another config field

boundedBootstrapAttempts.observed: the same entry completes in 2.2s instead of stalling, which pins the block to bundled plugin loading; but the bundled provider catalog goes with it, so the run fails with `Unknown model: openai/gpt-rc02-inbound (model_not_found)` and never reaches the model boundary
still stalls past 120s, so the allowlist does not prevent the full bundled load

boundedBootstrapAttempts.attempt: OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR pointing at a temp root with a junction to extensions/openai
boundedBootstrapAttempts.observed: rejected before running: the fs-safe root guard raises `Symlink escapes plugin root`, so a bounded plugin root cannot be built by symlink

boundedBootstrapAttempts.attempt: OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 plus explicit registration of the openai plugin's provider and modelCatalogProviders collections into the active registry
boundedBootstrapAttempts.observed: still `model_not_found`: the model catalog is not resolved from those registry collections, so explicit registration is not enough to make the configured model resolvable

followUpProbe.boundedBootstrapConclusion: the entry is drivable only when bundled plugin loading is fast or bounded AND the model catalog still resolves; neither the allowlist nor explicit registration achieves that today, so this row stays a gap until a bounded-bootstrap harness exists
followUpProbe.resolution: resolved 2026-09-23: with bundled discovery disabled the entry completes in about 2s, and the model catalog is satisfied by seeding the resolved agent models.json (resolveDefaultAgentDir + providers.openai) plus OPENAI_API_KEY for auth. The same recipe then drove every previously open surface: desktop chat and the channel fixture through dispatchInboundMessageWithBufferedDispatcher, cron through runCronIsolatedAgentTurn, and the CLI through agentCommand, so all eight named surfaces now have a real driver. Remaining narrowing: bundled plugin discovery is not exercised, the channel plugin layer is not exercised, and the compact half of the CLI/compact surface is not separately driven

probeAttempts.observed: no stdout for 120000ms with OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 and a minimal cfg; the watchdog terminated the stalled process group (the 90s per-test timeout never surfaced)
probeAttempts.conclusion: the only existing driver (run.test-harness.ts) mocks run-embedded.runtime.js, so it cannot prove the real entry; an unmocked driver stalls on the same runtime bootstrap

ownerClassification.claim: every persisted wire receipt carries a named adapter and provider and runtime_mode=source; the matrix fails if any row is unowned
ownerClassification.limitation: buildWireOwnerCensus currently assigns every final-body leaf to the named transport adapter; a per-field producer/transform split is not implemented, so this is an ownership-completeness check, not a field-level attribution map
